name: zog-b486cb1a-blind23-ots
instr:
# zog answers the wrong way round in a dozen places — diagnosing it without a test suite

Since updating, a great many everyday operations in this library come back with answers that are simply the reverse of what they used to be, and a few come back with nothing at all. The repository has received 23 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I have pinned down by exercising the public surface.

Checking one plain value against a built-in rule now often answers backwards. The rule for web addresses refuses `http://example.com` and accepts `not an address`, and its negated form mirrors that, accepting a real address and complaining about gibberish. The rule for dotted-quad numeric addresses is inverted the same way: `192.168.1.1` and `127.0.0.1` are refused while `256.1.1.1`, `not-an-ip` and the longer colon-separated forms are accepted. The e-mail and unique-identifier rules beside them still answer as they always did. An upper bound that should include its own limit no longer does: a rule permitting at most five now refuses exactly five, for whole numbers, unsigned ones, fractional ones and user-defined numeric types alike, while four still passes, six is still refused, and a lower bound still accepts its own boundary value.

Rules about how big a collection may be have stopped refusing anything. In an ordered collection, three elements pass a rule allowing at most two and one element passes a rule demanding at least two, so the exact-length rule built on those
